source: He, Panigrahi, Lin, Arora (2025) AdaptMI: Adaptive Skill-based In-context Math Instruction for Small Language Models
finding: Skill-matched worked examples help a small model on problems it fails, but add load and hurt on problems it already solves. The fix is to give them only after a failure (two stages). Authors link it to cognitive overload.
numbers: Five Qwen2.5 and Llama-3.x models, 1B to 7B. AdaptMI gains up to 3.6 points and AdaptMI+ up to 6 points over non-adaptive prompts. Qwen2.5-1.5B on MATH: 57.2 (AdaptMI+) vs 53.0 (skill-based).
limits: Math only (MATH, GSM8K); a reward model flags difficult questions; examples picked with GPT-4o-mini skill labels. Small models only.
agent_relevance: Direct match for a subgoal library: retrieve worked subgoal examples only after a check fails (fits G1, doubt only on a signal). Never inject by default.
quote: skill-based selection ... akin to cognitive overload

source: He, Panigrahi, Lin, Arora (2025) AdaptMI: Adaptive Skill-based In-context Math Instruction for Small Language Models (Table 2 detail)
finding: Skill-based examples raise accuracy on difficult questions and lower it on easy ones. This is an expertise-reversal-like pattern in a model.
numbers: Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct: easy-question accuracy drops about 5 to 13 points with skill-based vs fixed examples, by category (e.g. GSM8K easy 96.3 fixed vs 83.2 skill-based); average drop about 4 points across 5 SLMs on MATH easy questions. Difficult questions gain about +3 to +10.
limits: Table text parsed from PDF is partly garbled; direction and size are reliable, per-cell values less so.
agent_relevance: Add a gate: if a cheap first attempt passes a check, skip the worked example. Link to the expertise-reversal subfield.

source: He, Panigrahi, Lin, Arora (2025) AdaptMI: Adaptive Skill-based In-context Math Instruction for Small Language Models (iteration)
finding: Re-selecting examples each round, aimed at still-unsolved problems, keeps adding accuracy; random re-selection does not.
numbers: Iterative AdaptMI+ gains up to 7.2 points over iterations; most gain in the first four loops; the 7B model starts to decline by loop 10.
limits: Uses GPT-4o-mini as the example selector; 1.5B, 3B, 7B models.
agent_relevance: Library lookup can loop: fetch, try, check, fetch a different example. Cap loops at about 4.

source: Min et al. (2022) Rethinking the Role of Demonstrations: What Makes In-Context Learning Work?
finding: Demonstrations help mostly through format, label space and input distribution, not through correct input-output mapping. Random labels barely hurt.
numbers: 12 models incl. GPT-3. Replacing gold labels with random labels cost 0 to 5 points absolute; 1.7 on average in multi-choice, 2.6 in classification.
limits: Classification and multi-choice tasks; older models; not multi-step solving.
agent_relevance: Worked examples for LLMs may mainly set format and scope. Judge a subgoal library by what it changes in output, not by whether examples are fully right.
quote: replacing labels in demonstrations with random labels barely hurts

source: Wang et al. (2023) Towards Understanding Chain-of-Thought Prompting: An Empirical Study of What Matters
finding: Worked examples with invalid reasoning steps keep 80-90% of the chain-of-thought gain. Relevance to the query and correct step order matter more than step validity.
numbers: text-davinci-002. GSM8K answer accuracy: standard 15.4, CoT 48.5, invalid reasoning 39.5 (about 81% of CoT). Intrinsic recall retained over 90% of CoT.
limits: Human worked-example work says errors in examples hurt learners; models behave differently. Older model, GSM8K and Bamboogle.
agent_relevance: Library entries need relevance and step order more than perfection, but do not rely on errors being harmless: G3 still needs held-out checks.
quote: prompting with invalid reasoning steps can achieve over 80-90% of the performance

source: Wei et al. (2022) Chain-of-Thought Prompting Elicits Reasoning in Large Language Models
finding: Eight hand-written worked examples (question, steps, answer) in the prompt lift multi-step reasoning in big models. The LLM analogue of the worked-example effect.
numbers: PaLM 540B GSM8K: standard 17.9 vs chain of thought 56.9 (+39.0); +9.6, +1.8, +10.6, +14.2 on four other sets.
limits: Emerges only at scale (about 100B parameters); no load measures; fixed hand-picked exemplars.
agent_relevance: Baseline evidence that full worked solutions beat bare answers. Newer reasoning models differ (see R1 line).

source: Kojima et al. (2022) Large Language Models are Zero-Shot Reasoners
finding: One phrase (think step by step) with no examples gets much of the gain. Worked examples are partly replaceable by an instruction.
numbers: InstructGPT (text-davinci-002) zero-shot CoT: MultiArith 17.7 to 78.7; GSM8K 10.4 to 40.7.
limits: Few-shot CoT with good examples still beats zero-shot on harder sets in other papers.
agent_relevance: Cheap first move: ask for steps; add retrieved worked examples only if needed.

source: Yasunaga et al. (2024) Large Language Models as Analogical Reasoners
finding: Asking the model to recall and write its own relevant solved examples before solving beats 0-shot CoT and hand-written 5-shot CoT.
numbers: GSM8K with GPT-3.5-turbo: 5-shot CoT 75.0 vs self-generated 75.8 to 77.8; MATH gains of about 1 to 4 points; text-davinci-003 GSM8K retrieved CoT 54 vs self-generated 61.
limits: Table cells parsed from PDF are interleaved across models, so only direction is certain. MATH gain small.
agent_relevance: Self-made worked examples work for strong models. Gives a no-library option, but G4 warns the examples share the model's blind spots.

source: Yasunaga et al. (2024) analogical prompting: scale and count
finding: Self-generated examples help only when the model is strong enough. Weak models do better with retrieved examples. Best number of self-made examples is 3 to 5; one is worse.
numbers: GSM8K: text-curie-001 about 2-3% for all methods; text-davinci-002 retrieved 47 vs self-generated 48; text-davinci-003 retrieved 54 vs 61. K=1: 76.1; K=3 to 5: about 77-78.
limits: Old models; parsed table.
agent_relevance: Choose by model strength: external library for weak models, self-recall for strong ones. Use 3 examples, not one.

source: Agarwal et al. (2024) Many-Shot In-Context Learning
finding: Hundreds to thousands of examples beat few-shot. Model-written worked solutions (Reinforced ICL) beat human-written ones on MATH and transfer to GSM8K.
numbers: Up to 8192 shots. MATH500: Reinforced ICL plateaus near 25 examples and is about 5 points above ICL with human solutions; human-solution ICL peaks near 125 examples then declines. Minerva 4-shot: 55.7 MATH500, 90.6 GSM8K.
limits: Gemini 1.5 Pro; performance drops past an optimal count on some tasks (planning, verifier); cost linear in shots.
agent_relevance: Self-verified solutions make better library items than raw human ones. Filter by an answer check (supports G3). Count has an optimum.
quote: model-generated chain-of-thought rationales in place of human-written

source: Agarwal et al. (2024) Many-Shot ICL: unsupervised variant
finding: Problems alone, with no solutions, did about as well as problems with solutions on MATH. Solutions may be redundant when pretraining already covers the domain.
numbers: Unsupervised ICL matched or beat ground-truth-solution ICL at few- and many-shot on MATH500; Reinforced ICL beat Unsupervised on GSM8K transfer with at least 25 shots.
limits: Holds for math the model has seen; authors flag it may not hold in novel domains.
agent_relevance: The worked-example effect weakens for a model that already has the skill: same logic as expertise reversal.

source: Fu et al. (2023) Complexity-Based Prompting for Multi-Step Reasoning
finding: Choosing worked examples with more reasoning steps gives better results than simple or retrieved ones.
numbers: GPT-3 and Codex: average +5.3 and up to +18 accuracy points across GSM8K, MultiArith, MathQA, Date Understanding, Penguins; new SOTA on three math sets.
limits: Older models; part of the gain comes from voting over complex chains at decoding.
agent_relevance: For the subgoal library, store fully elaborated multi-step solutions, not terse ones.

source: Zhang et al. (2023) Automatic Chain of Thought Prompting in Large Language Models
finding: Diverse auto-built worked examples (one per cluster) resist errors; similar-question retrieval can import the same mistakes.
numbers: Unresolving error rate: retrieval-based 46.9% vs random 25.8%. With up to 50% wrong demonstrations Auto-CoT did not degrade much on MultiArith. Demonstrations by different annotators: up to 28.2% accuracy gap on a symbolic task; reordering changed under 2%.
limits: MultiArith, small experiments; Zero-Shot-CoT answers used as demonstrations.
agent_relevance: Retrieving the nearest example can copy a failure mode (G4). Pull diverse subgoal examples, not only the nearest.

source: Wang et al. (2023) Voyager: An Open-Ended Embodied Agent with Large Language Models
finding: An agent stores working code skills keyed by a description embedding and reuses them. Closest deployed analogue of a subgoal library in an LLM loop.
numbers: 63 unique items in 160 iterations (3.3x baselines). Wooden/stone/iron tool 15.3x / 8.5x / 6.4x faster than AutoGPT; only method to reach diamond (1 of 3 runs). Ablations: random curriculum -93% items; no self-verification -73%; GPT-3.5 for code 5.7x fewer items.
limits: Minecraft; skills are executable code verified by the game; GPT-4 needed; 3 trials.
agent_relevance: Store only verified items; the check matters (-73% without it).

source: Wang et al. (2023) Voyager: zero-shot generalization with and without library
finding: On new tasks in a fresh world the skill library is what lets Voyager solve them, and it also helps other agents.
numbers: Iterations (successes of 3): Voyager diamond pickaxe 19 (3/3), golden sword 18 (3/3), lava bucket 21 (3/3), compass 18 (3/3). Without library: 36 (2/3), 30 (3/3), 27 (3/3), 26 (3/3). ReAct, Reflexion, AutoGPT: 0/3 on all. AutoGPT with library: 1/3, 1/3, 0/3, 2/3.
limits: Three trials per cell; small N.
agent_relevance: Library gives roughly 1.4 to 1.9x speed-up on transfer tasks and plugs into other agents.

source: Wang et al. (2024) Agent Workflow Memory
finding: Agent learns reusable workflows from past successful runs and uses them as in-context guidance for new web tasks.
numbers: Relative success gains: Mind2Web +24.6%, WebArena +51.1%, with fewer steps. Advantage grows from 8.9 to 14.0 points as train-test gap widens. 1000+ tasks, 200+ domains.
limits: Only the abstract page was read; raw rates not seen. Web navigation only.
agent_relevance: Worked procedures help more when the new task is far from the old: supports a general subgoal library. Check on our own data.

source: Sarukkai et al. (2025) Self-Generated In-Context Examples Improve LLM Agents for Sequential Decision-Making Tasks
finding: An agent that keeps its own successful trajectories as examples beats handcrafted prompts. Curation by measured usefulness adds more.
numbers: ALFWorld 73 to 89; Wordcraft 55 to 64; InterCode-SQL 75 to 79 (gpt-4o-mini). Gain larger than upgrading to gpt-4o and matches multiple attempts. With population and exemplar-level curation, ALFWorld reaches 93.
limits: Abstract page read, not full text; three benchmarks.
agent_relevance: Strongest direct support: success-gated self-collected examples plus usefulness scoring. Score each stored subgoal by whether it helped.

source: Zhao et al. (2024) ExpeL: LLM Agents Are Experiential Learners
finding: Agent keeps success and failure trajectories plus extracted natural-language insights. Both example retrieval and insights are needed.
numbers: HotpotQA: ExpeL 39.0 +/- 1.7 vs insight-variant ablations of about 28 to 32; ExpeL 40% matches Reflexion 39% without repeated attempts. Insights extracted only from the original few-shot examples gave no advantage over ReAct.
limits: Ablation table garbled in PDF extraction, so variant numbers are approximate; ALFWorld figures unreliable.
agent_relevance: Worked examples plus a distilled rule beat either alone. Make rules from fresh experience, not from the prompt examples.

source: Yang et al. (2024) Buffer of Thoughts
finding: A library of high-level thought templates is retrieved per problem and filled in. A worked-example/subgoal library in LLM form.
numbers: Gains over prior SOTA: Game of 24 +11%, Geometric Shapes +20%, Checkmate-in-One +51%; 12% of the cost of multi-query methods. Removing the problem distiller lowers accuracy more on hard tasks than simple ones.
limits: Template buffer built from the same task families; Llama-3-70B and GPT-4.
agent_relevance: Distill the problem first, then retrieve a template. Fits a restate-then-retrieve step.

source: Cai et al. (2024) Large Language Models as Tool Makers
finding: A strong model writes a reusable function once; a cheaper model reuses it. Cached tools act as worked solutions.
numbers: GPT-4 as maker with GPT-3.5 as user keeps performance at lower cost on Big-Bench tasks (abstract). Exact per-task numbers not extracted.
limits: Only the abstract was read closely.
agent_relevance: Make once with the strong model, cache, reuse cheaply: a cost pattern for the library.

source: Shinn et al. (2023) Reflexion: Language Agents with Verbal Reinforcement Learning
finding: Verbal reflections from failed runs kept in memory serve as lessons for the next try.
numbers: HumanEval pass@1 91.0 vs GPT-4 80.1; reported gains over baselines: 22% AlfWorld, 20% HotPotQA, 11% HumanEval.
limits: Needs a real feedback signal (tests, environment).
agent_relevance: Matches G2: revise from real output. Store failure lessons next to success examples.

source: DeepSeek-AI (2025) DeepSeek-R1: Incentivizing Reasoning Capability in LLMs via Reinforcement Learning
finding: For this reasoning model, worked examples in the prompt make results worse. Authors advise a zero-shot prompt.
numbers: No number in the paper; one sentence: few-shot prompting consistently degrades performance.
limits: Single model family; no effect size; may not hold for other reasoning models.
agent_relevance: Reversal case: a model that already reasons may be anchored by examples. Test examples on vs off per model before fixing the schema.
quote: Few-shot prompting consistently degrades its performance.

source: Substack toy test (secondary): Few-Shot Prompting: Does It Really Degrade Model Performance?
finding: Small arithmetic test: few-shot hurt an RL-trained model but helped a supervised model.
numbers: RL model 85% zero-shot to 70% few-shot; supervised model 78% to 82% (as given in a search summary).
limits: Blog, small scale, not opened; weak evidence.
agent_relevance: Hint only; run our own test.

source: Pardos and Bhandari (2024) ChatGPT-generated help produces learning gains equivalent to human tutor-authored help on mathematics skills
finding: Randomized study with ChatGPT worked-solution style hints: gains equal to human tutor hints.
numbers: N=274, four algebra and statistics areas. Only the ChatGPT group had gains significantly above control; no ChatGPT vs tutor difference. 32% of ChatGPT help failed quality checks; near 0% for algebra and 13% for statistics after self-consistency.
limits: Not opened this session (search summary only). Hints, not full worked examples.
agent_relevance: LLM-made worked solutions need an answer check before use: about 1 in 3 were faulty. Supports G3 and G5.

source: Pardos and Bhandari (2023) preprint: Learning gain differences between ChatGPT and human tutor generated algebra hints
finding: Early version: ChatGPT hints had positive gains but only human-tutor hints were significantly better than control. Mixed result later superseded.
numbers: 77 MTurk participants who completed the lesson, 2x2 design. Human hints gave significantly higher gains than ChatGPT hints in both areas; about 70% of ChatGPT hints passed manual checks.
limits: Small N; the later N=274 study reversed the picture with better checks (a partial non-replication).
agent_relevance: GPT-3.5-era results were mixed: do not assume LLM worked solutions equal expert ones.

source: Jury et al. (2024) WorkedGen: LLM-generated interactive worked examples for programming
finding: Prompt chaining and one-shot prompting improved quality of generated programming worked examples. About 400 first-year Python students found them useful.
numbers: About 400 students; ratings only, no test-score gain.
limits: Search summary only; perceived usefulness, not learning.
agent_relevance: Quality came from prompt design, not from the model alone.

source: Hassany et al. (2024) Human-AI Co-Creation of Worked Examples for Programming Classes
finding: A system drafts line-by-line Java code explanations for instructors to edit, because instructors rarely have time to write them.
numbers: Abstract page read: no sample or rating figures on that page.
limits: Quality outcomes not seen.
agent_relevance: An LLM can draft the explanations and a human or check edits them.

source: United Minds or Isolated Agents? Exploring Coordination of LLMs under Cognitive Load Theory (CoThinker) (2025)
finding: Authors use cognitive load theory as a design lens for multi-agent LLM systems: spread intrinsic load, structure communication. Gains concentrate on reasoning-heavy tasks; overhead dominates on easy tasks.
numbers: Abstract page only; no figures extracted.
limits: An analogy to CLT, not a test of worked examples.
agent_relevance: Same pattern as AdaptMI: extra structure helps hard items and hurts easy ones.

source: Search gap record (this run)
finding: No controlled study found that compares worked-example prompts against problem-only prompts for an LLM using the human protocol (matched problems, load measures, transfer test). Closest are CoT vs zero-shot (Wei, Kojima), AdaptMI, and analogical prompting. Faded-example and completion-problem effects in LLMs not found.
numbers: WebSearch budget ran out after about 10 queries; OpenAlex was rate-limited and arXiv API returned nothing. Papers were fetched by known arXiv id.
limits: A real gap may exist or the search was too short.
agent_relevance: Our own test is needed: worked example vs completion problem vs bare problem on the same model, with a check.
